newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Chartists expect continuing dollar rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Chartists expect continuing dollar rally.

text.p: The dollar made a significant push versus the yen, hitting a fresh four-year high at 123.84 on Monday, but failed to extend the rally against the European currencies.
While the dollar rallied out of a recent triangle pattern against the yen, a dollar/mark triangle and an apparent head and shoulders pattern indicate upside pressure, technical analysts said.
"The dollar/yen triangle was resolved bullishly, but dollar/mark really hasn't broken out," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
"Dollar/mark still has some downside risk," Siller added.
Part of the dollar's problem is the surging British pound, which hit a 52-month high above 202 yen in midday trade.
With cable advancing more than two cents to a session high $1.6420 and a mark/yen rally boosting the German unit, the dollar slipped against the mark, pound and Swiss franc.
Chartists disagreed on whether dollar/yen or mark/yen held the key to the other's fate, but the two seem clearly linked.
"If dollar/yen has difficulty, mark/yen will have difficulty," said Joseph Klettner, foreign exchange technician at Chase Securities.
Dollar/yen faces few technical hurdles to 126, with a medium-term objective between 126.21, a high from January 1993, and 126.70, the high from August 1992.
But a yen slide could yield a break of mark/yen resistance at 75.20, which could weaken dollar/mark, chartists added.
Dollar/mark enjoys current support near 1.63, where a neckline to the apparent head and shoulders and rising trendline come in, analysts said.
"The short-term trend (higher) won't reverse unless we get a break below 1.63," Klettner said.
